title: Bananas (per lb)

drivers.name: Store closed Monday
drivers.evidence: Sales in 2025-10-12 (same week, Monday closed) were 17% below baseline. One past occurrence; noise-adjusted estimate shrunk.

adjustment.analysis: The store is closed Monday, reducing the week's operating days. Historical data shows a 17% drop in sales when the store is closed Monday (vs. same week last year, 2025-10-12). The price increase to $0.68 (+1.5%) is small and not expected to significantly impact volume, especially given the closed day. The classical uplift model's 1.00 multiplier is appropriate for no promotion, but the closure is a named driver. The noise-adjusted effect of a Monday closure is x0.83 (17% drop), supported by one past occurrence. We shrink toward 1.0 slightly due to limited data. No other drivers present.

  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 438.1 | 5%-95%: 313.1 - 555.4 | 10%-90%: 346.9 - 528.6

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-21% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
